findings.title: Walk 1's fingerprint stamp for its new MODIFIED block is an edit no sweep scope lists
findings.recommendation: The residual check (base file review-system-2026-10-04T16-41-51Z.json, added in d25d6429) lists .openspec.yaml, which no owed entry's file or ripple_cascade.applied names: walk 1's external C1 resolution added the `Engine-owned spine composition and filename discipline` MODIFIED block and stamped its base fingerprint (line 10), but its ripple record lists the delta and not the stamp. The stamp itself is correct (fingerprint --check: 6 verified). A record gap, not a defect — no edit needed; a walk that adds a MODIFIED block should list .openspec.yaml in its ripple_cascade.applied.

commentary: VERIFICATION over both walks of the blind pair. Each owed entry was graded over its sweep scope — the entry's file plus every ripple_cascade.applied path — reading the edit at HEAD plus the working tree: walk 1's cross-trail collision bump survived walk 2's second edit to emit-composition.ts; the base-file rule reads the same in the body and the delta, and walk 2's ordinary-case wording sits on top of it rather than replacing it; the verdict fence in the owner and its body mirror are held by the new parity test; the reverse-direction refusal text is pinned in both the engine and the body. Passes 1–3 ran over the union of the scopes; 4 and 5 have no lens files to read; 0 and 6 are whole-change and whole-project by the branch's own stated rule, so this pass did not run them. The residual check ran from d25d6429, the commit that added only the fresh pass's file, so both walks' edits were in range — the one listed file outside every scope is the fingerprint stamp, a record gap with a correct value.
